The existing implementations have different configs for browser and server so that you don't have to ship a shared entrypoint for browser Client and server Client. For example, `packages/react-server-dom-turbopack/src/client/react-flight-dom-client.browser.js` and `packages/react-server-dom-turbopack/src/client/react-flight-dom-client.node.js`.

I didn't see this decision in https://github.com/react/react/pull/36309 mentioned explicitly so I'm wondering if it was intentional or not.
Good call out! I would modify this package to ship 2 separate entrypoints for client and server

discussion_comments.comment_body:
( Nit / stylistic, feel free to disregard )

It's starting to feel that we're branching into many modes for `createResponseState`, with arguments that either (1) affect whether Fizz SSR has opted into a mode or (2) affect how Fizz behaves when in specific mode (e.g. `fallbackBootstrapScriptContent`)

I know that we prefer flat objects for perf reasons, and I can see why that would be useful for opaque objects that are read frequently e.g. `ResponseState`. However, would it be reasonable to change the interface for `createResponseState` and `renderIntoX` to use nested objects? These are only created / accessed once.

e.g. 
```
function createResponseState(
identifierPrefix: string | void,
  nonce: ...,
  bootstrapScriptContent: ...,
  bootstrapScripts: ...,
  bootstrapModules: ...,
  externalRuntimeConfig: ExternalRuntimeConfig | null,
  containerConfig: RenderIntoContainerConfig | null,
}
